summary: A revised set of ARPANET mailing lists for distributing network documents, replacing the one in RFC 329. List A lets sites reach network liaisons quickly with their own documents, while lists B and C are used by the Network Information Center for other participants and for station agents. It was replaced by RFC 402.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 363 updates three postal mailing lists for distributing network documents to liaisons, other participants and station agents. It replaced RFC 329 and was later replaced by RFC 402.

subtitle: Three revised mailing lists for distributing ARPANET documents

tldr.problem: The names and addresses used to distribute network documents needed another update.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC provides refreshed Lists A, B and C for liaisons, other network participants and NIC station agents.
tldr.outcome: RFC 363 replaced RFC 329 and was later replaced by RFC 402.

facts.label: Station-agent mailing frequency
facts.value: Once a week or more often when quantity warrants

sections.title: Updated Distribution Lists
sections.content:
RFC 363 provides three lists for distributing network documents. Sites use List A to send their own documents to liaisons quickly; all mail other than local mail should be sent by air mail.

The NIC uses Lists B and C to distribute copies to non-site network participants and station agents. The document obsoletes RFC 329 and supplies updated contact information.
sections.plainLanguage: The lists show where to send paper network documents. List A serves site liaisons, while Lists B and C serve other participants and station agents through the NIC.

sections.title: Liaisons and Other Participants
sections.content:
List A includes network liaisons and others who receive initial distribution of RFCs from the NIC or from sites. They also receive selected catalogs and other formal NIC documents.

List B identifies participants who receive formal NIC documents. The RFC lists names, organizations, postal addresses and telephone numbers for the recipients.
sections.plainLanguage: List A is for the initial recipients of RFCs and selected formal documents. List B is for other network participants who receive formal documents from the NIC.

sections.title: Station Agents and Replacement
sections.content:
List C names NIC station agents. They receive copies of documents distributed to liaisons and documents sent as part of a station collection. The NIC mails to station agents once a week, or more often when the quantity warrants.

The unit metadata records RFC 402 as the document that later obsoleted RFC 363.
sections.plainLanguage: List C identifies station agents who receive copies for their sites. RFC 402 later replaced this version of the list.

references.text: Stanford Research Institute, "ARPA Network Mailing Lists," RFC 329, May 1972.
